sentences.text: [1.1] By the said impugned judgment and award, though the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition preferred by the original claimant under Section 166 of the Act of 1988, holding him entitled to recover Rs. 5,88,400/-with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition, till its actual realization with proportionate costs, from the original opponents nos.1,2 and 3, who are held liable to pay 70% and opponent nos.4 and 5, who are held liable to pay 30%, the amount of compensation, jointly and severally; however, has not entertained the entire claim of compensation for sum of Rs.8 Lakhs.
Hence, the present appeal praying for enhancement of the amount of compensation to the extent of Rs.2 Lakhs with interest and proportionate costs.
[2.] Considering the grounds raised in the appeal and the submissions made by learned advocate for the appellant, this Court, vide order dated 15.06.2015, had admitted the appeal.
The record and proceedings have been called for.
The notice of admission of appeal is reported to have been duly served upon respondent nos.1 and 2, who are the driver and owner of another vehicle truck involved in the accident.

The notice of admission of appeal is reported to have been duly served upon the respondent no.3-Insurance Company of the NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined truck, who is represented by learned advocate Mr. Ankit Shah.

[3.] With the able assistance of learned advocates appearing for the respective parties, the appeal is finally heard and decided by this judgment.

[4.] Mr. R.K. Mansuri, learned advocate for the appellant- original claimant, at the outset, has submitted that the present appeal is confined mainly on the quantum of compensation being determined on the lower side.

It is submitted that though the issue of negligence has not been disputed in the present appeal; however, even accepting the contributory negligence of the claimant to the extent of 30% as determined by the Tribunal, he is entitled to recover the amount of compensation to the aforesaid extent from the owner and the Insurance Company of the Jeep, who are joined as respondent nos.4 and 5 respectively in the present appeal.

sentences.text: Referring to the facts of the case, learned advocate has submitted that the claimant was 30 years of age and was employed as a manager in a private company.
Because of the motor vehicle accident, he had suffered grievous injuries including fracture of the left leg, facial injuries, and a severe head injury.
He had undergone prolonged treatment and had suffered permanent disability at 65%.

It was pleaded by the claimant that because of the aforesaid injuries, his functional capacity and earning potential have been substantially NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined impaired.
Before the Tribunal, considering the injuries sustained and the medical case papers, the loss of future earning capacity was computed on the basis of 63% disability.
Being aggrieved, the insurer had approached in appeal, contending that the compensation awarded was excessive and disproportionate to the injuries sustained.
The High Court, upon re-appreciation of evidence on record, observed that the Medical Board had assessed the physical disability of the claimant at 63%.

Upon independent evaluation of the nature of injuries and the impact of such injuries on the claimant's avocation as a Manager, the High Court adjudged the functional disability of the claimant at 30% instead of 63%
and had thereby partly allowed the appeal, reducing the amount of compensation.

The claimant was,
therefore, constrained to approach in appeal before the Hon'ble Supreme Court, mainly on the issue of disability being assessed incorrectly.

It was specifically contended that having regard to the nature of brain injuries and its consequences, the amount of compensation is required to be re-computed by treating it as a case of 100% functional disability.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, upon re- appreciation of the evidence on record, did not approve the findings and reasons assigned by the High Court, in the absence of convincing evidence impeaching the credibility of the medical certificates placed on record by the claimant and without assigning cogent reason, found NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined such conclusion of disability, confined to 30% as not justified.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court independently evaluated the true nature and extent of injuries and its impact on the cognitive and functional abilities of the claimant.

The Court, in principle, followed its earlier decision in the case of Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar reported in 2011 (1) SCC 343 and, has fixed the disability of the claimant as 100% for the purpose of computing loss of earning capacity.
[4.4] Learned advocate has also prayed for enhancement of the amount of compensation under the head of pain, shock, and suffering from Rs. 50,000/- to Rs. 5,00,000/- considering that initial accidental injuries exacerbated, resulting in the eventual amputation of the right hand of claimant.

[8.] At the outset, it is required to be noted that, 
pointed out by the learned advocate for the appellant, as regards the issue of negligence vis-a-vis the involvement of the vehicle, the accidental injuries sustained by the claimant due to the motor vehicle accident, and the liability of the driver/owner/insurer of the other vehicle (truck) involved in the accident being not disputed, have attained finality.

It is also required to be noted that, though the respondent no.5- Insurance Company has disputed its liability to pay the amount of compensation for the first time being raised in the present appeal, the fact remains that the respondent no.5-Insurance Company has neither preferred any cross-appeal nor any cross- objections disputing their liability to pay the amount of compensation.

[9.] On the issue of quantum of compensation, the core contention, which is raised by the learned advocate for the claimant, is the disability of the claimant being assessed as 70% instead of treating it as a case of 100 % functional disability of the claimant.
The claimant has entered the witness box, and his examination-in-chief- affidavit has been produced on record at Exh. 44.

He has specifically deposed before the Tribunal that, because of the motor vehicle accident, while he was sitting in the driver's seat of the Jeep, he had sustained injuries on his right shoulder, which was completely crushed, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined and his right hand was lost.
Apart from the aforesaid injury, he has also suffered a fracture in his leg and has sustained injuries on the head and other parts of the body.
He was immediately shifted to the Vatrak Civil Hospital, and thereafter, was shifted to Ahmedabad Civil Hospital, where he was treated as an indoor patient for a period of one month.
The operation was performed and he had lost his right hand.
It was further submitted that,
having
lost his right hand, he is unable to drive the vehicle and has thereby lost his sole source of livelihood.
It has been specifically deposed before the Tribunal that because of the amputation of his right leg, he is unable to attend his daily chores and is completely relying upon his family members.
He is unable to enjoy the conjugal rights of his matrimonial life.
He has, therefore, prayed for compensation of Rs.8 Lakhs under various heads.

In support of his aforesaid case, the claimant has produced on record the medical case papers, which includes the injury certificate at Exh. 50 issued by the Medical Officer, Civil Hospital, Ahmedabad, and the disability certificate issued by Dr.
Prafulla N. Shah, MS (Ortho) at Mark 21/03.
The X-ray report has also been produced on record at Exh.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid documentary evidence, in light of the evidence of the claimant, the Tribunal has failed to apply the settled principles with regard to the assessment of functional disability in a case of amputation.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Raj NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined Kumar (supra)
, has laid down the principles to be borne in mind, while assessing the permanent disability for the purpose of determination of loss of future earnings.
The Courts/Tribunals have been cautioned not to mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

The Supreme Court has emphasized that the Tribunals are effectively required to take into consideration the earning capacity of the injured, and after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of the percentage of the income, are required to quantify in terms of money.
The three steps guided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court are required to be thus applied in the peculiar facts of the case.
[10.] Indisputably, the claimant was engaged in driving and was earning his livelihood from the aforesaid avocation.
With the loss of the right hand, it is apparent that the claimant is unable to earn his livelihood by doing the job of driving.

Thus, it can be considered as a case of total disablement,
as he would not be able to effectively carry out the activities and functions, which he used to earlier carry, because of the injuries sustained.
He has been prevented from discharging his previous activities and functions, as can be gathered from his evidence on record.

The decision in the case of Raj Kumar (supra), has been affirmed subsequently in various decisions, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined including the recent judgment of the Supreme Court in the case of R. Halle (supra) as relied upon by the learned advocate for the appellant.

[11.] Bearing in mind the aforesaid principles, the Supreme Court reverting to the facts of the case on hand, has independently evaluated the evidence and has noted that, since the impairment strike at the core competencies indispensable for the effective discharge of managerial responsibilities and substantially undermining the claimant's ability to perform the essential functions inherent in such a position, has reckoned the disability at 100%.

Applying the aforesaid principles in the facts of the case, this Court has no hesitation in accepting the case of the claimant to be treated as 100%
functional disability.

[12.] Having held so, considering the minimum wages of Rs. 2,900/- as notified by the State Government and prevailing at the time of the accident i.e. on 25.04.2008, applying the well-settled principles laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), treating it as a case of salaried person below the age of 40 years, addition of 40% is required to be considered for the purpose of determination of the future prospective income of the claimant.
Thus, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined

considering the fact that the age of the claimant is considered between the age group of 25 to 30 years by the Tribunal, in absence of any challenge being made, the multiplier of 17 has rightly been applied.
Considering the aforesaid components, the future loss of income is re
- determined as Rs.1,160/- (Rs. 2,900/- x40%).

Accordingly, the prospective income of the claimant is fixed as Rs. 4,060/- per month (Rs. 2,900/- +
Rs. 1,160/-).
The future loss of income is re- determined by treating it as a case of 100% functional disability as Rs. 8,28,240/- (Rs. 4,060/- x 12 x 17).

[13.] Having held so, as regards the amount of compensation under the other heads are concerned,
admittedly the claimant has suffered amputation of his right hand.
The accident had taken placed place on 25.04.2008.
The injury certificate produced on record suggests that he was shifted to Ahmedabad Civil Hospital on 26.04.2008 and was thereafter, treated as an indoor patient and was discharged on 26.05.2008.
The injury certificate suggests that he has suffered crush injury with amputation on his right shoulder.
There was a comminuted fracture noted in the upper part of the lateral border of the scapula with glenoid.

Considering the aforesaid injury certificate in NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined light of the X-ray report dated 04.07.2008 produced on record at Exh.56, it can be noticed that a disarticulated shoulder is noted and the fracture of the scapula is also confirmed.
Though, there is no erosion or osteomyelitis noted, the fact remains that the claimant has suffered not only physical agony but mental agony as well with regard to the nature of the injury sustained.

Considering the ratio laid down by the Supreme Court in cases of Mohd. Sabeer (supra) and Pappu Deo Yadav (supra) and, considering the amputation of his right hand whereby the claimant would be unable to lead a normal life as he was leading prior to the accident, the amount of compensation under the head of "Pain, Shock, and Suffering" is redetermined as Rs. 2,00,000/-.

Similarly, the amount of compensation is also required to be reconsidered under the head of "Loss of Amenities" and is determined as Rs.
2,00,000/-.

Considering the fact that the claimant was aged 29 years and the longevity of the life of the claimant, whereby the claimant would be required to incur future expenses towards an artificial limb, the amount of compensation under such expenses is determined as Rs. 5,00,000/-.
[14.] It is required to be noted that the claimant has not disputed the negligence as determined by the Tribunal.
On the other hand, the opponents have also chosen not to dispute the issue of negligence.

The only issue, which has been disputed by respondent no.

opennyai_summary.facts:
Upon independent evaluation of the nature of injuries and the impact of such injuries on the claimant's avocation as a Manager, the High Court adjudged the functional disability of the claimant at 30% instead of 63%
and had thereby partly allowed the appeal, reducing the amount of compensation.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court, upon re- appreciation of the evidence on record, did not approve the findings and reasons assigned by the High Court, in the absence of convincing evidence impeaching the credibility of the medical certificates placed on record by the claimant and without assigning cogent reason, found NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined such conclusion of disability, confined to 30% as not justified.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court independently evaluated the true nature and extent of injuries and its impact on the cognitive and functional abilities of the claimant.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Though, it is a case of amputation of the right Ishwaribhai Babubhai Raval vs Harshadbhai Ranchhodbhai Brahmbhatt on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85180584/
5 hand, the claimant is able to perform his other activities, as it is not the case of the claimant that he is completely dependent on his family or is bedridden.
It is the disability certificate produced by the claimant himself, wherein the doctor, upon evaluation of the medical case papers and upon clinical examination of the claimant, has opined it to be a case of 70% permanent disability of the right hand.
opennyai_summary.issue:
[7.] Before adverting to the merits of the appeal, it would be appropriate to note that the only issue,
which arises for consideration of this Court in the present appeal is, as to whether the Tribunal committed any error in quantifying the amount of compensation while deciding a claim petition preferred under Section 166 of the Act of 1988, in the facts of the case and the evidence on record?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Considering the aforesaid documentary evidence, in light of the evidence of the claimant, the Tribunal has failed to apply the settled principles with regard to the assessment of functional disability in a case of amputation.
The three steps guided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court are required to be thus applied in the peculiar facts of the case.
[10.] Indisputably, the claimant was engaged in driving and was earning his livelihood from the aforesaid avocation.
With the loss of the right hand, it is apparent that the claimant is unable to earn his livelihood by doing the job of driving.
Thus, it can be considered as a case of total disablement,
as he would not be able to effectively carry out the activities and functions, which he used to earlier carry, because of the injuries sustained.
He has been prevented from discharging his previous activities and functions, as can be gathered from his evidence on record.
Applying the aforesaid principles in the facts of the case, this Court has no hesitation in accepting the case of the claimant to be treated as 100%
functional disability.
[12.] Having held so, considering the minimum wages of Rs. 2,900/- as notified by the State Government and prevailing at the time of the accident i.e. on 25.04.2008, applying the well-settled principles laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), treating it as a case of salaried person below the age of 40 years, addition of 40% is required to be considered for the purpose of determination of the future prospective income of the claimant.
Thus, NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/326/2015 JUDGMENT DATED: 06/04/2026 undefined
considering the fact that the age of the claimant is considered between the age group of 25 to 30 years by the Tribunal, in absence of any challenge being made, the multiplier of 17 has rightly been applied.
Considering the aforesaid components, the future loss of income is re
The future loss of income is re- determined by treating it as a case of 100% functional disability as Rs. 8,28,240/- (Rs. 4,060/- x 12 x 17).
The amount of compensation towards actual loss Ishwaribhai Babubhai Raval vs Harshadbhai Ranchhodbhai Brahmbhatt on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85180584/
8 of income is required to be adjusted under the head of loss of future income, in the facts of the case.
[13.] Having held so, as regards the amount of compensation under the other heads are concerned,
admittedly the claimant has suffered amputation of his right hand.
Learned advocate for respondent no. 5- Insurance Company has fairly conceded to the fact that no appeal or any cross- objections has been filed by the said Insurance Company, assailing the impugned judgment and Ishwaribhai Babubhai Raval vs Harshadbhai Ranchhodbhai Brahmbhatt on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/85180584/
9 award of the Tribunal.
[15.]
In absence of any evidence suggesting the revocation of the policy, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the findings and reasons assigned by the Tribunal with regard to the negligence vis-a-vis the liability of the respective Insurance Companies of the vehicles involved in the accident.
